clinician.trajectory_summary: A 24-year-old sexually active homosexual male presented with five days of acute painless progressive bilateral vision loss (visual acuity 20/600 bilaterally) and recent alopecia. Ophthalmology examination revealed bilateral vitritis with white tufts and globular white opacities consistent with posterior uveitis. Inpatient workup demonstrated cerebrospinal fluid pleocytosis (WBC 33 cells/μL), elevated protein (44 mg/dL), and positive Venereal Disease Research Laboratory (VDRL) titer of 1:2, confirming neurosyphilis. CSF studies were negative for fungal, mycobacterial, Lyme, Bartonella, and viral hepatitis etiologies. MRI of the brain and orbits was normal. The patient was newly diagnosed with HIV infection (CD4 count 1347 cells/μL, viral load 52,900 c/mL). Treatment with a 14-day course of intravenous penicillin G was initiated in the emergency department.
